top_choice_rationale: Targeted protein degradation (Crews, Deshaies, Handa) is one clearly stated mechanism: a small molecule enforces proximity between a chosen protein and an E3 ligase, so inhibition is replaced by removal. It is a new, general capability, independently reproduced, with a molecular mechanism for both the PROTAC and cereblon branches. The three-name allocation matches priority (concept and demonstration, and the cereblon target of thalidomide). The main costs are the pending clinical record and the omission of Ciulli. Ionizable lipid nanoparticles come second for their proven clinical impact but unsettled credit among six names. C-N coupling is mature but closer to a refinement of the 2010 paradigm. No award is last because several candidates are clearly prize-worthy.
